title: Understanding Homoeopathy: A Gentle Approach to Healing
author: Dr. Ananya Sharma
excerpt: Homoeopathy treats the person, not just the symptom. Know how this gentle system of medicine works and what makes it different.
content:
Homoeopathy is a natural system of medicine developed more than two centuries ago. Its central idea is simple: like cures like. A substance that can produce symptoms in a healthy person may, in a highly diluted form, help relieve similar symptoms in someone who is unwell.

A personalised approach

Two people with the same complaint may need entirely different remedies. A homoeopathic practitioner looks at your physical symptoms, sleep, appetite, mood and general constitution before suggesting a remedy. This is why self-medication is best kept to minor, well-understood complaints.

Gentle by design

Remedies are prepared through a process of serial dilution and succussion. The final preparation is generally well tolerated, including by children and elderly patients, when chosen appropriately.

  • Remedies are usually given as small globules or tablets.
  • Take them away from food, tea and coffee where possible.
  • Always follow the advice of a qualified practitioner for ongoing complaints.

At Homeokit Homoeopathy, we believe good health begins with understanding. Explore our guides to learn more about remedies, potencies and everyday wellness.

title: 5 Homeopathic Remedies for Common Cold & Seasonal sniffles
author: Dr. Ananya Sharma
excerpt: A practical guide to commonly used remedies for cold, sneezing and congested sinuses — and how to tell them apart.
content:
Seasonal changes often bring along sneezing, a runny nose and that familiar blocked feeling. Homoeopathy offers several remedies, and the right one depends on how your symptoms behave.

Commonly considered remedies

  • Allium Cepa: watery nasal discharge that irritates the upper lip, with frequent sneezing.
  • Nux Vomica: cold with chilliness, body aches and digestive disturbance.
  • Euphrasia: irritation of the eyes along with a bland nasal discharge.
  • Kali Bichromicum: thick, stringy mucus and sinus pressure.
  • Gelsemium: slow onset, heavy eyelids and weakness with feverish feeling.

Simple care while you recover

Rest, warm fluids and saline steam can make a big difference. If symptoms last more than a week, worsen suddenly, or are accompanied by high fever, please consult a doctor.

title: How to Choose the Right Potency: 30C, 200C or 6X?
author: Rohit Menon
excerpt: Potency can feel confusing. Here is a simple explanation of the numbers you see on every homoeopathic bottle.
content:
If you are new to homoeopathy, the numbers on the label can look mysterious. Potency simply tells you how many times a substance has been diluted and succussed.

What the numbers mean

  • 6X / 6C: lower potencies, often used for mild, local complaints and cell salts.
  • 30C: the most commonly used potency for acute, everyday complaints.
  • 200C and above: higher potencies, usually reserved for cases guided by a practitioner.

A few practical tips

Do not change potency frequently. Give the remedy time to act, and avoid repeating a dose unless advised. Keep remedies away from strong smells, sunlight and moisture so they stay effective for longer.

When in doubt, speak to a qualified homoeopath — the right remedy at the right potency makes all the difference.

title: Skin Care the Natural Way: Calendula & Beyond
author: Dr. Ananya Sharma
excerpt: Discover how calming botanicals like Calendula fit into a simple, gentle daily skin care routine.
content:
Healthy skin usually starts with simple habits: gentle cleansing, enough water, sun protection and a little patience. Botanicals such as Calendula can be a useful addition.

Why Calendula?

Calendula officinalis, or marigold, has a long history of use in natural skin care. It is commonly included in ointments for minor cuts, dry patches and irritated skin.

A gentle routine

  • Cleanse with lukewarm water and a mild cleanser.
  • Pat dry — never rub harshly.
  • Apply a thin layer of a soothing ointment where needed.
  • Use a simple moisturiser and sunscreen during the day.

Persistent rashes, itching or acne deserve a proper consultation. Natural care works best when it is matched to your skin.

title: A Beginner's Guide to Mother Tinctures
author: Rohit Menon
excerpt: Liquid plant extracts, explained. What they are, how they are used and what to keep in mind before buying one.
content:
Mother tinctures are liquid extracts made from plants, minerals or other natural substances. They are the starting point from which homoeopathic potencies are prepared.

How are they taken?

Typically, a few drops are diluted in water and taken two or three times a day. Because they are less diluted than tablets, they can have a stronger taste and a more direct action.

Things to remember

  • Shake the bottle well before every use.
  • Use the measuring dropper provided — more is not always better.
  • Store in a cool, dark place, tightly closed.
  • Consult a practitioner for long-term use, pregnancy or for children.

Our Mother Tinctures range is prepared with care and sealed with clear labelling, so you always know exactly what you are using.
